title: MCP Phase 3 Content-Light Output Scanning Implementation v1 — Rig Relay
files_changed: rig_relay/protocols/mcp/server.py (imported redaction primitives, added _classify_mcp_output and _scan_tool_output, integrated scan into call_tool and call_tool_sync dispatch paths)
scanner_selected: rig_relay/evidence/redaction.py — canonical Rig Relay redaction module. Uses _FORBIDDEN_FIELD_KEYS (47 forbidden field names), _SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS (5 regex patterns for sk-*, bearer, private keys, api keys), _SENSITIVE_NAME_PATTERNS (15 sensitive field name patterns).

output_classifications.public_safe: No secrets, no forbidden keys, no private paths. Returned normally with content_light_classification tag.
output_classifications.private_local: Contains cwd or absolute path metadata. Returned with classification tag; may be refused by future local policy.
output_classifications.sensitive_metadata: Contains token-like keywords (access_token, bearer, authorization, api_key) but no actual secrets. Metadata-only refusal.
output_classifications.secret_bearing: Matches _SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS — contains actual secret fragments (sk-*, bearer tokens, private keys). Refused.
output_classifications.forbidden_raw: Contains keys from _FORBIDDEN_FIELD_KEYS (raw_file_contents, source_code, diff, api_key, stdout, stderr, etc.) or token-like content. Refused.

scan_integration_points: call_tool(): after _dispatch() returns, before result assembly and persist
call_tool_sync(): after _dispatch_sync() returns, before result assembly and persist
All tools (async + sync): scan runs after descriptor integrity and root boundary checks, before response serialization

remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_4_evidence_envelopes: No common ReceiptEnvelope wrapping for MCP outcomes. Responses carry content_light_classification but lack other envelope fields (session_id, trace_id, envelope_id, etc.).
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_5_auth: MCPPerUserAuthorization model exists but not enforced. No per-session token required.

mcp_security_implications.before: MCP read-only tools inside workspace root could return arbitrary output including secret-bearing content, API keys, raw file contents, or private paths. Content-light was advertised but never verified.
mcp_security_implications.after: Every MCP tool output is classified before serialization. Secret-bearing and forbidden-raw outputs are refused with structured refusal envelopes. Public-safe outputs carry explicit classification. Refusals never echo the detected secret. Scan runs after descriptor integrity and root boundary (defense-in-depth order).
